title: Extension Request Window for Work Conditioning and Work Hardening Programs
content:
# Extension request window

For the hour-billed programs of the Workers' Compensation Referral, the request window is the number of whole weeks an extension asks the adjuster to cover.

**Window rule.** The request window is one (1) week (the final block) where fewer than two whole weeks remain before the program's maximum length, counted from the initial evaluation; three (3) weeks where two or more whole weeks remain, no missed program day with a date of service in the last month has been reported to the adjuster and the latest progress report was sent to the adjuster no more than one progress-report interval before the request; and two (2) weeks otherwise.

## Terms

- **Initial evaluation** — the date of service of the referral's evaluation charge.
- **Whole weeks remaining** — the program's maximum length in days (its maximum length in weeks multiplied by seven) less the calendar days from the initial evaluation to the request, divided by seven and rounded down to a whole number.
- **Latest progress report** — the latest progress report sent to the adjuster on the referral; where none has been sent, the time is counted from the initial evaluation.

## Program figures

| Program | Maximum length | In days | Progress-report interval |
|---|---|---|---|
| Work Conditioning Program | 6 weeks | 42 | 14 calendar days |
| Work Hardening Program | 8 weeks | 56 | 7 calendar days |

## Decision table

| Whole weeks remaining | Missed program day reported, last month | Latest progress report within one interval | Request window |
|---|---|---|---|
| fewer than 2 | any | any | 1 week |
| 2 or more | none | yes | 3 weeks |
| 2 or more | one or more | any | 2 weeks |
| 2 or more | none | no | 2 weeks |

## Cases (hypothetical, Work Conditioning Program)

- Initial evaluation 28 days before the request: 42 less 28 is 14 days, which is 2 whole weeks. No missed day reported last month and a progress report sent 10 days before: 3 weeks.
- Initial evaluation 29 days before: 13 days, which rounds down to 1 whole week: the final block of 1 week.
- Initial evaluation 20 days before: 42 less 20 is 22 days, which is 3 whole weeks. The latest progress report was sent 16 days before the request, more than one 14-day interval: 2 weeks.
